stories.headline: UAE Foreign Minister conducts intensive diplomatic outreach on Iran war across multiple capitals
stories.summary: Sheikh Abdullah bin Zayed held a series of bilateral calls and in-person meetings this week with counterparts from the US, Russia, UK, Netherlands, Canada, Kuwait, and Finland, in each case discussing the Iran war, regional de-escalation, and bilateral ties. A formal UK-UAE joint statement was published on April 25 jointly condemning Iran's attacks on the UAE and GCC states.

stories.headline: India NSA Doval meets UAE President MBZ in Abu Dhabi to strengthen strategic partnership
stories.summary: Indian National Security Adviser Ajit Doval visited Abu Dhabi on April 26 and met with UAE President Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, conveying greetings from Prime Minister Modi and discussing the India-UAE Comprehensive Strategic Partnership, energy security, and the regional situation amid the Iran war. The meeting was also attended by Abu Dhabi Crown Prince Sheikh Khaled bin Mohamed.

stories.headline: UAE navigates Iran war fallout: debate on US bases, censorship of attack footage, and official messaging
stories.summary: The week saw sustained coverage of the UAE's domestic and public posture following Iranian missile and drone attacks, including: a debate triggered by an Emirati academic arguing US military bases are no longer strategic assets; the UAE ambassador to the UK defending arrests of individuals who filmed and shared attack footage; and official narratives projecting the UAE as a resilient 'beacon of peace.' A senior official confirmed the UAE is 'not on the sidelines' of Iran ceasefire negotiations.

stories.headline: UAE-US currency swap talks emerge as CBUAE governor seeks dollar liquidity backstop; UAE warns of yuan oil sales if dollars run dry
stories.summary: Reports emerged this week that CBUAE Governor Khaled Mohamed Balama proposed a currency swap arrangement with US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent at IMF/World Bank meetings. President Trump said the deal was 'under consideration.' The UAE Embassy in Washington pushed back, asserting the country holds over USD 2 trillion in assets and does not require assistance. Separately, Emirati officials reportedly warned Washington privately that prolonged dollar shortages could force oil sales in Chinese yuan, the most serious challenge to the petrodollar since the 1970s according to one analyst.

stories.headline: MBZ receives Syrian President Al-Sharaa on working visit to Abu Dhabi
stories.summary: Syrian President Ahmed Al-Sharaa arrived in Abu Dhabi on April 22 for an official working visit and was received by UAE President Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed. The two leaders discussed bilateral cooperation, economic ties, regional security, and ongoing developments in the Middle East. Al-Sharaa was greeted upon arrival by Foreign Minister Abdullah bin Zayed.

stories.headline: Israel secretly deployed Iron Dome battery and IDF operators to UAE during Iran war — first-ever operational export of the system
stories.summary: Israeli and international media reported this week that Israel sent an Iron Dome battery along with several dozen IDF operators to the UAE during the Iran war, following a call between Prime Minister Netanyahu and President MBZ. The deployment is described as the first time Iron Dome has been used operationally outside Israel or the United States.

stories.headline: ADNOC defers LNG to India, Sultan Al Jaber conducts field visits, and launches bp hydrogen JV amid Hormuz crisis
stories.summary: ADNOC Gas opted to defer LNG cargo deliveries to Indian buyers rather than declare force majeure as the Strait of Hormuz remains near-closed. ADNOC CEO Sultan Al Jaber conducted a series of field visits to key operational sites including the Shah Sour Gas Plant to review readiness. ADNOC and bp also formally launched a joint venture for large-scale hydrogen and carbon capture projects in the UAE and UK. Separately, Sultan Al Jaber publicly called for Hormuz to be 'returned to the world' via a post on X.

stories.headline: Spanish pipe manufacturer Tubacex reports severe disruption to billion-euro ADNOC contract due to Iran war
stories.summary: Basque tube manufacturer Tubacex reported a sharp drop in first-quarter 2026 profits and is considering temporary layoffs after the Iran war disrupted logistics to its Abu Dhabi plant and the flow of orders under its approximately €1 billion, 10-year ADNOC contract. The company's new Abu Dhabi facility had been expected to drive significant growth in 2025-2026.

stories.headline: CBUAE reports Emiratisation in financial sector hits 31%, exceeding 2025 targets
stories.summary: The Central Bank of the UAE reported that UAE nationals now represent 31% of employees across banking, financial, and insurance sectors, with 23,364 Emirati staff — exceeding 2025 targets. The CBUAE highlighted partnerships with federal and local entities including an 'Al Ain Initiative' that achieved a 60% employment rate for its 2025-2026 goals.
